text: According to Chapter 1, when the book asks “What is time?” in its intended philosophical sense, it is primarily asking:
choices: How time behaves — how it relates to space, velocity, energy, and gravitational fields
What kind of thing time is — its nature — a question that physics uses time to do but does not itself answer
How to construct more accurate clocks so that temporal intervals can be measured
Whether the word “now” is grammatically an indexical of the same kind as “here”
explanation: Chapter 1 sharply separates the physics of time (how time behaves) from the philosophical question of its nature (what kind of thing it is), insisting that 'physics uses time; it does not explain it.' Describing time's behavior is exactly the question the book sets aside; clock-building is measurement; and the grammar of 'now' is a narrower Chapter 2 topic, not the central question posed here.
